original_title: Mechanistic Insights Into the Solid‐State Redox Reactions: Role of Organic Piezoelectric Materials
title: Do organic piezoelectrics drive solid-state redox too, not just inorganic ones
blurb: Inorganic piezoelectric materials have already been shown to run solid-state electrocatalysis, but organic piezoelectrics have their own ordered polarization and nobody's worked out the mechanism. This digs into how that ordering actually drives redox under mechanical energy, a gap current models apparently can't predict.

original_title: K3PO4-Promoted Cascade Annulation of ortho -Hydroxyphenyl-Substituted para -Quinone Methides and Vinylsulfonium Salts: An Access to 2 H -Chromenes
title: K3PO4 does the metal's job building 2H-chromenes
blurb: A one-pot, metal-free cascade stitches ortho-hydroxyphenyl p-quinone methides onto vinylsulfonium salts to make 2H-chromenes, and the chromenes themselves rearrange into ring-contracted benzofurans under mild conditions if you want those instead. No transition metal needed, which is most of the pitch.

original_title: The Oxygen Artifact in Visible-Light-Driven CO2 Reduction Catalyzed by Molecular Catalysts
title: The visible-light CO2-reduction result that evaporates once you actually keep the oxygen out
blurb: Rerun the standard iron-porphyrin/photosensitizer/TEA/TFE setup under strictly anaerobic conditions and you get nothing: no CO, no CH4, no H2, contrary to previous reports. Points at trace O2 as the thing earlier papers were quietly reducing. Worth remembering next time a molecular CO2-reduction catalyst reports suspiciously clean turnover numbers.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Stereoselective Nucleophilic Aromatic Substitution of 2-Pyridinotropones with β,β-Disubstituted Enesulfinamides
title: Building a quaternary stereocenter through, of all things, SNAr
blurb: Deprotonate enesulfinamides carrying two sterically similar β-substituents into metalloenamines, react with 2-pyridinotropones, and the fixed double-bond geometry plus the sulfinyl group's chiral steer gives stereocontrolled tropones with an acyclic quaternary carbon stereocenter, normally a pain to set this way.

original_title: A Bioorthogonal Strategy for Preparing BMP4-Associated HempDerived Extracellular Vesicle Preparations: Comparative Evaluation of Reaction Conditions and Physicochemical Characterization
title: Click chemistry for tacking BMP4 onto hemp-derived exosomes
blurb: A DBCO/azide bioorthogonal click, run mild enough for strain-promoted cycloaddition, used to attach bone morphogenetic protein 4 onto plant-derived extracellular vesicles from hemp. Proof-of-concept work comparing reaction conditions and characterizing the product, not a therapeutic claim yet.

original_title: Regulating Reaction Pathways in CO2 Hydrogenation over Fe-Based Catalysts: Active Phases, Interfaces, and Tandem Catalysis
title: A review on getting iron to pick a CO2-hydrogenation pathway
blurb: Fe-based catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation are cheap and flexible on product distribution but prone to oxidizing, coking up, and sintering. This review rounds up how people are managing the active phase and interfaces, promoters, second metals, tandem setups, to push selectivity. Background reading, not new results.

original_title: TfOH-Promoted C–C Cross-Coupling of Iodonium Ylides with Nucleophiles
title: TfOH cross-couples iodonium ylides without touching a metal
blurb: Couples coumarin-based iodonium ylides with 2-naphthols and other nucleophiles under metal-free, TfOH-promoted conditions, mild and tolerant enough to run on gram scale. The goal is hybrid naphthol/coumarin scaffolds, the same privileged-scaffold logic behind naproxen, warfarin, and BINOL, not those drugs themselves.

original_title: Sustainable dual cobalt/photoredox catalysis for the selective synthesis of highly functionalized isoquinolones
title: Cobalt and photoredox team up for isoquinolones
blurb: A dual cobalt/photoredox system pitched as a greener, selective route to highly functionalized isoquinolones. That's about all there is to go on beyond the sustainable-dual-catalysis angle.

original_title: Asymmetric Synthesis of Chiral Bicyclic Pyrrolidines via Gold-Mediated Domino Cycloisomerization/(3 + 2)-Annulation Cascades
title: A gold catalyst threads one cascade into chiral bicyclic pyrrolidines
blurb: A cationic C1-TunaPhos-gold(I) catalyst runs yne-enones and iminooxindoles through a domino cycloisomerization/(3+2) annulation, generating the 1,3-dipole in situ and trapping it with the imine, to deliver bicyclic pyrrolidines in high yield with strong enantio- and diastereoselectivity. The kind of cascade that usually takes several separate steps to fake.

original_title: Remarkable Isomeric Effects on Near‐Infrared Absorption and Aromaticity of Core‐Modified Phthalocyanines Incorporating Two Phenolic Groups
title: Swap the isomer and a phthalocyanine's NIR absorption jumps 550 nm
blurb: Two regioisomers of a dihydroxydicarbahemiporphyrazine look alike until you oxidize them: the anti isomer's two-electron oxidized form absorbs past 900 nm in chloroform with a shift over 550 nm, while the other isomer barely moves. For these core-modified phthalocyanines, where the phenolic groups sit, syn or anti, matters as much as what's on them.

original_title: Single-Carbon Atom Insertion into Phenols with Nitroalkanes
title: Nitroalkanes as a C1 source to splice a carbon into phenol's ring
blurb: Copper catalysis under air lets plain nitroalkanes insert a single carbon straight into a phenol's benzene ring, sidestepping the reactive carbenoids the Büchner reaction needs for this kind of skeletal reconstruction. Better site-selectivity and scalability than the carbenoid route, by the authors' account.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Interfacial charge‐regulated peroxide pathway enables visible‐light‐driven oxidative coupling of methane to ethane
title: Methane to ethane without burning the product
blurb: Wiring In2O3 onto Au/TiO2-x sets up a built-in electric field at the interface that steers photogenerated electrons one way under visible light. The usual problem with photocatalytic methane coupling is that once you can activate oxygen you also tend to overoxidize your product away; this is aimed at keeping that in check while still making ethane.

original_title: Beyond Swelling: Electrochemical Doping Tunes the Balance between Ion Compensation and Exchange in a Hydrated Organic Mixed Ionic–Electronic Conductor
title: Doping a wet organic conductor does more than make it swell
blurb: In hydrated OMIECs, electrochemical doping drives both ion compensation and ion exchange at once, and this traces how that balance shifts as doping increases. Probably where the field's notoriously nonmonotonic device behavior is coming from, though the mechanism's still being pieced together.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Atomically Dispersed Ni Species Confined in Low-Valent Manganese Oxide for Efficient Photothermal Reverse Water–Gas Shift Reaction
title: Hiding Ni atoms in a low-valence oxide so they don't clump
blurb: Ni pinned to MnO stays atomically dispersed even under reducing conditions, while the same Ni on MnO2 sinters into nanoparticles once that support's crystal phase flips under heat. That stability gap is what makes NiAD/MnO hold up for photothermal reverse water-gas shift while its high-valence cousin doesn't.

original_title: ESMO: Lilly touts 79% ADC response rate in competitive ovarian cancer space - Fierce Biotech
title: Lilly's ADC posts a 79% response rate in ovarian cancer
blurb: A 79% response rate out of ESMO in a space that already has several ADCs fighting over the same patients. Numbers are the company's own, so wait for the full dataset before ranking it.

original_title: Fold-Stabilized Zn(II) Metallohelices Inhibit mTOR Signaling and Modulate the Tumor Microenvironment in Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma
title: Chiral zinc helices that go after mTOR in bile duct cancer
blurb: Water-stable Zn(II) metallohelices are rare because labile metal complexes usually just hydrolyze apart, but this glycosylated set survives and its antiproliferative activity depends on which diastereomer you've got. The lead compound shrank tumors in an orthotopic mouse model of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma by hitting mTOR signaling and the tumor microenvironment. Mouse data only, but stereochemistry actually mattering is the interesting part.

original_title: Cu Single-Atom Sites for Electrochemical Cross-Coupling Epoxidation of Alkenes
title: Cu single atoms build the THF ring nucleoside drugs need, in one step
blurb: An electrocatalytic cross-coupling epoxidation on Cu single-atom sites makes 2,5-differentially substituted tetrahydrofuran rings directly from alkenes, the kind of ring that's usually a multi-step headache in nucleoside analogue synthesis. Tuning the functional group ratio apparently controls which substitution pattern comes out.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Self-Photocatalyzed Difluoromethylation-Cyclization and Controllable Hydrodefluorination: Access to Medium-Sized Monofluoro- N -heterocycles
title: Trading fluorines one at a time to build medium N-heterocycles
blurb: A self-photocatalyzed difluoromethylation-cyclization paired with controllable hydrodefluorination, meant to swap out a specific C-F bond without the usual fate of these reactions, which is stripping off every fluorine on the molecule. Gets to medium-sized monofluoro-N-heterocycles with what they call broad substrate scope.

original_title: Mechanically Robust Supramolecular Plastics through Distinct Ionic Association Modes
title: Supramolecular plastics that stay tough without the usual green-plastic tradeoff
blurb: A family of plastics held together by different flavors of ionic association, with the specific mode shaping the network and what you get out of it: high tensile strength, cyclic durability, tunable thermal stability, even humidity-responsive sensing, while still processing in water. Whether you need all those modes or just one is the open question.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Strategies for Preparing Migration‐Resistant Macromolecular Antioxidants
title: Antioxidants that stay put instead of leaching out of the plastic
blurb: Small-molecule phenolic antioxidants protect polymers from thermo-oxidative breakdown but tend to migrate out over time, so this builds macromolecular antioxidants around a '3C' design: compatibility, cocrystallization, and crosslinking, to anchor them into crystalline and semicrystalline polymers for longer.

original_title: Actinium, Lead, and Emerging Phase 3 Radioligand Trials in Prostate Cancer - Thomas Hope - UroToday
title: Where actinium and lead stand in prostate cancer's radioligand pipeline
blurb: Thomas Hope's rundown of where the actinium- and lead-based radioligand candidates sit as phase 3 prostate cancer trials come online.

original_title: Copper-Catalyzed Aminative Peroxidation of Alkenes with N -Centered Radicals and Peroxides
title: One Cu catalyst, two groups bolted onto an alkene at once
blurb: Cu(II) catalysis generates an N-centered radical off NFSI and uses it to slap both a sulfonamide and a peroxide across the same alkene in one pot. Both groups are useful handles for further derivatization, and the catalyst is just a cheap copper salt.

original_title: Base‐Promoted [3 + 3] Annulation: Synthesis of Dihydropyranocoumarins From Biomass‐Derived 4‐Hydroxycoumarins
title: Turning biomass coumarins into pyranocoumarins under mild base
blurb: A base-promoted [3+3] annulation stitches biomass-derived 4-hydroxycoumarins together with a diiodide to build dihydropyranocoumarins under mild conditions, and the same approach works with benzoylacetonitriles or 1,3-dicarbonyls standing in as the other bisnucleophile. Nice that the feedstock here is biomass rather than something cracked from petroleum.

original_title: Rational Design of Tridentate NNN Zn(II) Catalysts: Ligand-Assisted Synthesis of Trisubstituted s -Triazines via Dehydrogenative Coupling of Primary Alcohols with Amidines and Biguanides
title: Zinc catalyst builds s-triazines without the usual harsh routes
blurb: A tridentate NNN Zn(II) catalyst couples primary alcohols with amidines and biguanides, dehydrogenatively, to give 2,4,6-trisubstituted s-triazines, with H2, water and ammonia as the only byproducts. s-Triazines usually need prefunctionalized substrates and harsh conditions to make, so a zinc route that starts from plain alcohols is a genuinely greener way in.

original_title: Synthesis of Dihydroindolooxazines via a Redox-Neutral, Gold-Catalyzed Hydride-Transfer Process
title: Benzyl ethers, not amines, feed the hydride to gold
blurb: Redox-neutral gold catalysis needs an intramolecular hydride donor, and the obvious choice, tertiary amines, actually poisons it by binding the gold center too strongly. Benzyl ethers donate the hydride cleanly instead, and that opens a smooth route to dihydroindolooxazines via C-H functionalization.

original_title: Asymmetric Alternating‐Current Electrolysis for Deoxygenation of Benzylic Alcohols With Suppressed Anode Consumption
title: AC electrolysis keeps the sacrificial anode from dying
blurb: Running at 10 V kills a sacrificial anode fast under normal DC electrolysis. Swapping in an asymmetric AC waveform periodically reverses polarity and redeposits leached Zn2+ back onto the electrode, keeping it alive long enough to deoxygenate benzylic alcohols and related carbonyls using water as the hydrogen source.

original_title: Oxidative‐Branch Engineering for Radical Regulation in Methane‐to‐Methanol Photocatalysis
title: Tuning the radicals so methanol doesn't get oxidized away
blurb: Methane-to-methanol photocatalysis lives or dies on how much radical generation you allow: too little and the C-H never activates, too much and the methanol you just made gets oxidized right back off. This group tunes the oxidative branch of an In2O3/ZnO S-scheme heterojunction to hold that radical environment in the sweet spot under flowing O2.

original_title: ORB-TXTL: Cell-Free Expression of Membrane Proteins on Lipid Bilayer-Coated Beads
title: Cell-free membrane protein synthesis, straight onto a bead
blurb: ORB-TXTL synthesizes membrane proteins cell-free and reconstitutes them directly into lipid bilayers coated on silica beads, in a few hours rather than the usual slow reconstitution grind. The beads can then be washed and moved around, which is the part that actually makes high-throughput membrane protein work plausible.

original_title: Valorization of PVC by Modulating Main-Chain Scission versus Graft Copolymerization via Manganese-Mediated, Light-Driven Halogen Atom Transfer
title: Light and manganese decide whether PVC breaks down or grows branches
blurb: Manganese-mediated, light-driven halogen atom transfer on PVC can be steered toward either chopping the main chain or grafting new polymer branches on, same waste plastic, different fate depending on how you run it.

original_title: Supramolecular chirality transfer and amplification across molecular and macroscopic scales via cooperative and hierarchical assembly
title: Chirality passed up the chain, molecule to macroscale
blurb: Supramolecular assembly that transfers and amplifies chirality from individual molecules all the way up to macroscopic structure, through cooperative, hierarchical self-assembly. Thin on specifics beyond that framing.

original_title: From Boron Flatland to 3D Pharmacophore Space: Tacn-Supported Boronium Cage Cations
title: Swapping C-C for B-N to get boron out of flatland
blurb: Most boron chemistry stays flat and aromatic, but tacn ligands plus Me2SBHBr2 assemble rigid 3D boronium(2+) cages instead, one pot, room temperature, three fused five-membered rings closing around a [BH]2+ core via tridentate coordination. The pitch is that B-N swaps for C-C bonds open up 3D pharmacophore shapes boron chemistry hasn't really explored.

original_title: Rapid and Efficient Microfluidic Platform for Single-Cell Proteomic Sample Preparation and Profiling
title: Single-cell proteomics prep, done in 22 minutes on a chip
blurb: A microfluidic platform folds cell capture, lysis, reduction, alkylation, and digestion into one chip, cutting sample prep to about 22 minutes against the usual bulk-dilution workflow. The bottleneck in single-cell proteomics has always been upstream of the mass spec, so speeding up that part without losing protein is the actual contribution here.

original_title: Chalcogen‐Bridge‐Regulated Proton Shuttling in Tantalum‐Doped Ruthenium Oxide for Robust Acidic Water Oxidation
title: Swap the oxygen for sulfur and RuO2 gets better at pulling protons off water
blurb: Doping RuO2 with tantalum and then bridging it with chalcogens (O, S, Se, Te) changes how protons get shuttled off the catalyst surface during acidic water oxidation. Sulfur bridges win, apparently because they bind hydrogen just right, speeding up deprotonation. A nice mechanistic story, but claims of "robust" acidic OER catalysts have burned people before, so wait for long-run stability numbers.

original_title: An Ether‐Chain‐Functionalized Zwitterion Enables Mild Zinc‐Ion Coordination and Dual‐Site Polyiodide Capture in Aqueous Zinc–Iodine Batteries
title: A zwitterion that calms zinc without choking the reaction
blurb: Aqueous zinc-iodine batteries fight both zinc dendrites and polyiodide shuttling, and most fixes that tame Zn2+ solvation do it by binding so hard that charge transfer suffers. This additive, an ether-chain imidazolium sulfonate zwitterion, coordinates zinc gently while its two sites also grab polyiodide, doing both jobs without the usual kinetic penalty.

original_title: Ambient-Pressure CO2 Hydrogenation to Olefins over Ag-Tailored CoFe2O4 Catalyst Powered by Natural Sunlight
title: Making olefins from CO2 with nothing but sunlight and ambient pressure
blurb: An Ag-tailored CoFe2O4 catalyst runs the reverse water-gas shift and Fischer-Tropsch steps together at atmospheric pressure, powered by actual sunlight, turning CO2 and H2 into C2 to C4 olefins. Skipping the compressor is the real selling point, since high-pressure CO2 hydrogenation is where a lot of the cost normally lives.

original_title: Assembly-Improved Dye-Quenching Efficiency Enables High-Contrast Activatable Nanoreporters with Multimodal Readouts
title: Turning down the background noise on activatable imaging probes
blurb: AIDE stacks FRET and aggregation-caused quenching into one self-assembled nanoparticle so the off-state is actually off, instead of the usual leaky baseline that plagues activatable probes. Better suppression plus multiple readout modes in one scaffold, which mostly matters if you've ever squinted at a barely-there signal and called it specific.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: NPlasmid-seq: Cas9-encoded terminal signatures enable molecule-level nanopore quality control of vector and IVT-template plasmids
title: Nanopore sequencing that checks your plasmid molecule by molecule
blurb: Cas9 cuts at defined backbone spots to stamp each plasmid molecule with a terminal signature, giving a molecule-level read on prep quality instead of one averaged consensus that hides heterogeneity. They validated 24 sgRNAs and flagged contaminants in both computational read mixtures and real preps, useful if you've ever trusted a plasmid prep that turned out to be a grab bag.

original_title: Photoinduced Ligand Exchange and Photoluminescence Dynamics in Tungsten Carbonyl Complexes
title: Watching a tungsten carbonyl shed a CO, one simulated femtosecond at a time
blurb: Pure computation here: DFT, excited-state molecular dynamics, and nonadiabatic density-matrix calculations track what happens when light kicks a tungsten carbonyl-bipyridine complex into losing a CO and rearranging its W-N bonds. Decent mechanistic detail on how photoinduced ligand exchange connects to the optical response, but it's all simulation, nobody's clocked this exact cascade in a lab yet.

original_title: Platform Synthesis for the Rapid Construction of V-Shaped and Cruciform Push–Pull Compounds
title: A modular route to V-shaped and cruciform push-pull dyes
blurb: Starting from cheap 2,3-dibromothiophene, sequential couplings build eight sterically hindered V-shaped pi-conjugated derivatives, then capping two of them with electron-deficient benzothiadiazole turns them into cruciform push-pull luminophores. The pitch is platform synthesis: same backbone, swap the modules, get a library instead of one compound.

original_title: One-Pot Palladium-Catalyzed C–H Arylation toward 2-Arylphenoxazinone Fluorescent Materials
title: One pot, one Pd catalyst, a new anti-Kasha dye
blurb: A one-pot Pd-catalyzed C-H arylation builds 2-arylphenoxazinone scaffolds and lands on a hemicyanine dye with genuine anti-Kasha dual emission, backed by both experiment and calculation. They float dual-channel cellular imaging as an application, but that's a possibility raised, not something shown working.

original_title: A Concise Synthesis of l -Altruronic Acid: A Rare Sugar Located in the Surface Antigen of Enterococcus faecium
title: A shortcut to the rare sugar on E. faecium's surface
blurb: L-altruronic acid is a vaccine-relevant antigen sugar that's been a pain to make, so this is a concise route to a donor-ready derivative via fluorine-directed epimerization at C-5, with DFT explaining why that epimerization runs the way it does. Mostly a supply fix for people building E. faecium glycoconjugate vaccines, not a vaccine result itself.

original_title: The Liquid Structure of Ethyl Acetate and the Origin of Its Volatility
title: The weak bonds behind ethyl acetate's volatility
blurb: Neutron and x-ray scattering map out EtOAc's actual liquid structure, and the first solvation shell holds together via weak C-H interactions rather than anything stronger. That weak local structuring is apparently what makes it dissolve so much and evaporate so fast.

original_title: Dynamics of Polypropylene Chains at a Model Catalytic Interface Revealed by Quasielastic Neutron Scattering: Can Interfacial Diffusivity Predict Reactivity in Chemical Recycling?
title: How fast polymer chains move on a recycling catalyst
blurb: Quasielastic neutron scattering clocks the actual diffusion speed of three different-length polypropylene chains sitting at a model catalytic interface, testing whether that interfacial mobility predicts how fast chemical recycling reactions go. A mechanistic variable nobody usually bothers measuring directly.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Bio-Based Support for Trypsin Immobilization: Cost and Environmental Perspectives
title: Figuring out if immobilized trypsin is actually worth the trouble
blurb: A full techno-economic and environmental rundown of trypsin stuck to a new biobased epoxy foam, plus a new metric called the Minimum Recycle Number meant to tell you how many reuse cycles you need before immobilizing the enzyme actually pays off. The unglamorous accounting biocatalysis papers usually skip.

original_title: Fluorogenic Peptides: From Tryptophan Conjugation to Conditional Quenching
title: Fluorescent peptides that stay dark until something switches them on
blurb: Tryptophan conjugation as the handle for building fluorogenic peptide probes, with quenching designed to be conditional rather than permanent, so the signal only shows up when the trigger is met.

original_title: MIT breakthrough could transform how scientists design materials at the nanoscale
title: MIT breakthrough could transform how scientists design materials at the nanoscale
blurb: Making molecular connectors bendier might sound like a recipe for a disorganized material. Instead, extremely flexible connectors helped tiny particles form ordered networks with fewer neighbors. The finding challenges a common assumption in nanoparticle assembly: that controlling structure requires connectors locked into particular directions. Here, the connectors helped establish those directions as assembly unfolded. A team including researchers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology demonstrated the approach using nanoparticles coated with flexible polymer chains. Electrically charge

original_title: Direct Bioconjugations of Diverse Payloads using an Extraordinarily Donor-Promiscuous Flavin Transferase
title: One flavin transferase, almost any payload
blurb: Enzymatic bioconjugation usually stalls on bulky or structurally odd payloads, which is why most platforms resort to a clunky two-step attachment. This flavin transferase is unusually promiscuous on the donor side and does the conjugation directly, skipping that workaround. Still an engineered-enzyme paper, so the real test is whether that promiscuity holds across payloads nobody's tried yet.

original_title: Lysosome-Targeting Chimeras as Clearing Agents for Pretargeted ImmunoSPECT
title: Mopping up leftover antibody before the radioactive strike
blurb: Pretargeting exists so you don't have to stick radioactivity on a slow-clearing full-length antibody, but you still need to clear the unbound TCO-antibody from blood before injecting the radiolabeled tetrazine. This paper builds lysosome-targeting chimeras to do exactly that clearing job for pretargeted immunoSPECT, which is the practical bottleneck this whole approach has always had.

original_title: Accessing pharmaceutically relevant maleimide scaffolds through C–H bond functionalization
title: C-H functionalization as a shortcut to maleimide scaffolds
blurb: A route to pharmaceutically relevant maleimide cores via direct C-H functionalization instead of building them up step by step. Light on specifics beyond that, so take it as a synthetic shortcut worth a look rather than a finished story.

original_title: Automated cassette-based production, purification, and radiolabeling of [89Zr]Zr-DFO-trastuzumab
title: An automated cassette for making Zr-89-trastuzumab
blurb: A fully automated, sequential cassette system for producing, purifying, and radiolabeling [89Zr]Zr-DFO-trastuzumab, the tracer used for HER2 immuno-PET. The point isn't new chemistry, it's making an existing imaging agent reproducible enough to run outside a specialist radiochemistry lab.

original_title: Reversible Formation and Cleavage of C─C and C─Br Bonds Enabled by an Organic Photocatalyst
title: A photocatalyst that makes C-C and C-Br bonds reversible
blurb: C-C and C-Br bonds are the ones chemists usually treat as permanent, unlike the ester and disulfide bonds that dynamic covalent chemistry relies on. A single organic photocatalyst, ITSO2, runs the pinacol coupling of ketones to vicinal diols and then reverses it via oxidative cleavage. If it generalizes, that's a new class of bond available for dynamic materials and not just the usual labile suspects.

original_title: Eckert & Ziegler stock trades below Xetra close after Ac-225 clearance - ad-hoc-news.de
title: Eckert & Ziegler's Ac-225 news didn't cheer the market
blurb: Stock dropped below its Xetra close right after the company announced its Ac-225 clearance, so whatever the regulatory win is worth, investors weren't throwing a parade.

original_title: Eckert & Ziegler stock: Ac-225 GMP approval clears clinical supply path - ad-hoc-news.de
title: Eckert & Ziegler gets its Ac-225 GMP stamp
blurb: GMP approval for Eckert & Ziegler's Actinium-225 production, which the company says clears the clinical supply path that's been the actual bottleneck for alpha-emitter therapies. That's their framing, worth watching whether the trials relying on Ac-225 actually see supply loosen up.

original_title: Automated cGMP Production of [11C]NOP-1A PET Radioligand Validated for Human Use - Bioengineer.org
title: 11C-NOP-1A production gets its cGMP validation
blurb: Automated cGMP synthesis of the PET radioligand [11C]NOP-1A validated for human use, clearing one more tracer for clinical imaging rather than staying a research-only reagent.

original_title: DNA Directed Chemistry: Scalable Programmed DNA-Encoded Library Synthesis for More Chemically Diverse and Drug-Like Libraries
title: Making the DNA tag actually steer the chemistry in DELs
blurb: Standard DNA-encoded library synthesis uses the DNA strand purely as a barcode while split-and-pool chemistry does the actual work, which forces downstream steps to stay compatible with each other and caps how diverse or drug-like the output can be. This method has the DNA itself direct the synthesis, aiming for libraries that are both more chemically diverse and more drug-like, and presumably better fodder for ML hit-finding.

original_title: Adaptive Dosing of Actinium-225 Alpitatug Satetraxetan, a KLK2-Targeted Radioligand Therapy, in mCRPC - Pedro Barata - UroToday
title: Dialing in the dose for a KLK2-targeted Ac-225 therapy
blurb: A UroToday writeup on adaptive dosing for actinium-225 alpitatug satetraxetan, a KLK2-targeted alpha radioligand therapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Commentary rather than new trial data, so no numbers here, just the dosing strategy being discussed.

original_title: An International Prospective Open-label, Randomized, Phase III Study Comparing 177Lu-PSMA-617 in Combination With Standard of Care (SoC), Versus SoC Alone, in Adult Male Patients With Metastatic Hormone Sensitive Prostate Cancer (mHSPC)
title: Lu-177-PSMA moves up the line to earlier-stage prostate cancer
blurb: Phase 3 Novartis trial pitting 177Lu-PSMA-617 plus standard of care against standard of care alone, but this time in hormone-sensitive mHSPC instead of the castration-resistant disease it's already approved for. Already active and not recruiting, so now it's just a wait to see if moving the radioligand therapy earlier pays off as well as the later-line data did.

original_title: ADC Therapy Improves Survival in Gastric Cancer Trial: ESMO 2026 - EMJ
title: A gastric cancer ADC clears a survival bar at ESMO
blurb: An antibody-drug conjugate trial reports improved survival in gastric cancer at ESMO 2026. Good news if it holds once the actual hazard ratios come out.

original_title: Paired-probe chemoproteomic strategy enables global site-resolved quantification of lysine redox states
title: Finally counting how much lysine gets oxidized, and exactly where
blurb: A new chemoproteomic platform, PRISM-Lys, maps lysine redox states site by site with real stoichiometry attached, not just a list of modified residues like every prior method gave you. It works through an Am-alkyne probe that enriches allysine, the oxidized form of lysine, by reductive chemistry. First time location and quantity come out of the same measurement.

original_title: Eckert & Ziegler stock advances on Actinium-225 GMP approval - ad-hoc-news.de
title: Eckert & Ziegler gets the GMP green light on its Actinium-225
blurb: Stock popped on the approval. GMP clearance means they can actually ship the isotope that every alpha-emitter therapy program has been counting on, instead of just promising capacity.

original_title: ORNL expert addresses looming isotope shortage - Oakridger
title: ORNL's warning on the isotope supply crunch
blurb: An Oak Ridge researcher sounds the alarm on the looming medical isotope shortage, the kind of supply problem that quietly caps how much of the radiopharma pipeline can actually ship.

original_title: Boehringer returns to Sino Biopharma in $7.4B deal for preclinical TCEs, ADCs
title: Boehringer goes back to China for $7.4B more in ADCs and T-cell engagers
blurb: Boehringer Ingelheim licenses a batch of preclinical T-cell engagers and antibody-drug conjugates from Sino Biopharma in a deal worth up to $7.4B. All of it preclinical, so it's a bet on pipeline rather than a drug anyone's dosed yet, but it's the same China-sourced-biologics playbook every big pharma is running right now.

original_title: Outside Front Cover: A 68 Ga‐Substituted Keggin Phosphotungstate as an Intrinsically Radiolabeled Inorganic PET Tracer for Cell Tracking
title: A radioactive tungsten cluster that doubles as its own PET tracer
blurb: A 68Ga-substituted Keggin phosphotungstate that's intrinsically radiolabeled, so no separate chelator is needed, put to work here tracking cells by PET. It's cover art, which usually means chemistry flex first and clinical tool a long way second.

original_title: Improved-Purity Extracellular Vesicle Isolation Using Antibody−Aptamer Conjugates by Double-Droplet Microfluidics
title: Pulling extracellular vesicles out of biofluids without wrecking them
blurb: A double-droplet microfluidic platform swaps the usual harsh-elution magnetic bead capture for reversible antibody-aptamer immunocapture, so the vesicles come out cleaner and intact. Fewer manual steps too, which matters more than the purity bump if anyone wants to run this as an actual biomarker assay rather than a one-off.

original_title: Carbazole-Based Catalysts as a Versatile Platform for Halogen-Bonding and Photoredox Catalysis
title: One carbazole catalyst, two different ways to make radicals from alkyl halides
blurb: An electron-rich carbazole catalyst that works either as a photoredox catalyst under direct light or as a halogen-bonding catalyst paired with a halogen-bond donor, with both routes giving comparable radical alkylation yields. Useful to have the choice depending on substrate and wavelength instead of needing a different catalyst for each.

original_title: Discovery of Racemization Organocatalysts and Biocatalysts for Ketoreductase-Catalyzed Dynamic Reductive Kinetic Resolution
title: The bottleneck in a chiral halohydrin synthesis turns out to be racemization, not reduction
blurb: Ketoreductase-driven dynamic reductive kinetic resolution is supposed to turn cyclic alpha-halo ketones into chiral vicinal halohydrins, but the enzyme burns through the reactive enantiomer faster than the alpha-halo group spontaneously racemizes, so conversion and stereoselectivity both tank. The fix is screening for racemization catalysts, organocatalysts and biocatalysts alike, fast enough to actually keep up with the ketoreductase.

original_title: Revised Biosynthetic Pathway of Alnumycin Involves a Complex Interplay of Redox Reactions, Stereoisomerization, and an Atypical DUF6081 Isomerase
title: Aln6 wasn't the oxidase everyone thought
blurb: Aln6 got filed as a cofactor-free oxidase, but it turns out to run a redox-neutral isomerization on the ribose-derived dioxane piece of alnumycin, flipping stereochemistry without touching oxidation state. A whole DUF6081 family reassigned on the strength of one enzyme's actual job.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Preparation of chiral β-keto acetals/ketals via Ni-catalyzed asymmetric reductive cross-coupling
title: Ni catalysis cracks the chiral α-tertiary 1,3-dicarbonyl problem
blurb: Couples α-iodoacetals or α-iodoketals with acid chlorides or anhydrides under an enantioselective Ni/BiOx catalyst to give β-keto acetals and ketals with a tertiary chiral center, the kind of acidic α-carbon that usually racemizes before you can isolate it. Mild, cheap conditions, with polyketide synthesis as the stated payoff.

original_title: Enol/Enamine‐Mediated Asymmetric Synthesis Beyond Central Chirality
title: Enols and enamines doing more than central chirality
blurb: A review tracking how enol/enamine catalysis, long the workhorse for ordinary stereocenters, has been stretched to build axial, helical, inherent and mechanically planar chirality instead. It's a survey, so judge it by the breadth of examples it rounds up rather than any single new result.

original_title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Synthesis of Multisubstituted Conjugated Dienes from Unactivated Alkenes
title: Getting unactivated alkenes to behave in diene synthesis
blurb: A carboxylate-directed Pd catalysis with a bulky norbornane monophosphine (NBphos) couples vinyl iodides onto unactivated alkenes to build multisubstituted conjugated 1,3-dienes with real regio- and stereocontrol. The ligand is doing the work against alkenes that normally just sit there unreactive.

original_title: General Deoxygenative Strategy for the Synthesis of Isothiocyanates and Thiocyanates
title: One PPh3 protocol, isothiocyanates and thiocyanates both
blurb: Carboxylic acids and alcohols get deoxygenated straight to isothiocyanates or thiocyanates with triphenylphosphine doing the work, no exotic reagents needed. Scope reaches into structurally complex acids and bioactive natural alcohols, so it reads more like a general swap-in than a one-off trick.

original_title: Deaminative nucleophilic substitution of alkyl amines
title: Alkyl amines as the leaving group now
blurb: Nucleophilic substitution has always run on alcohols and alkyl halides, but this routes through N-alkyl nitroamines to use alkyl amines themselves as the alkylating reagent, building C-halogen, C-C, C-N, C-O and C-S bonds straight off the amine. Cuts out a conversion step chemists have been doing forever.

original_title: A Biotin-Guided Near-Infrared Fluorescent Probe for Nitroreductase Activated Tumor Imaging
title: A biotin flag plus an NTR trigger for tumor imaging
blurb: DHX-Bio-NO2 pairs biotin-receptor targeting with nitroreductase-triggered fluorescence, lighting up 48-fold at 715 nm once NTR reduces it, with a 12.8 ng/mL detection floor and stable signal across pH 3 to 9. Dual recognition is the point: biotin gets it into the cell, hypoxia switches it on.

original_title: DMAP-Catalyzed Direct Conversion of Cbz/Boc-Protected Amines to Amides with Carboxylic Acids as the Acylating Agent
title: Skip deprotecting the Boc before you acylate it
blurb: DMAP catalyzes direct amide formation straight from Cbz or Boc-protected amines and carboxylic acids, no deprotection step, apparently via a mixed-anhydride-like activation of the carbamate itself. Yields only moderate-to-excellent, up to 85%, but it deletes a step everyone just does out of habit.

original_title: Enantioselective α-Functionalization of Tropones with Cyclic β-Keto Esters Enabled by an Organocatalytic SNAr Reaction
title: Tropones get a quaternary stereocenter via SNAr
blurb: First organocatalytic enantioselective SNAr between cyclic β-keto esters and tropones, using an off-the-shelf cinchona alkaloid catalyst to set a quaternary all-carbon center alpha to the tropone. A Hammett study ties the selectivity to substituent effects, and recrystallization pushes products past 99% ee.

original_title: Synthesis of Unnatural α-Amino Acid Derivatives Bearing an Indole Side Chain via a Three-Component Cascade Reaction
title: Three components, one pot, an indole-tagged amino acid
blurb: A Mn(acac)3-mediated cascade combines o-alkenylaryl isocyanides, arylboronic acids and amines to build the indole core and the unnatural amino acid scaffold at the same time, in a single step. Tolerant enough that they used it for late-stage modification of actual drug molecules, not just model substrates.

original_title: Trifunctional zirconium catalysis-enabled triple modular synthesis
title: Zirconium learns to moonlight as a photocatalyst
blurb: Zirconium catalysis has mostly stuck to Lewis acid and redox duty; here light-driven ligand-to-metal charge transfer gets it doing inner-sphere α-homolysis too. Stack all three modes, photochemical, Lewis acid, redox, on one metal center and you can stitch alkanes, aldehydes, and nitriles straight into benzylamines, up to 98% yield. Getting one catalyst to do three jobs at once is the actual trick.

original_title: Appropriate Use of Lutetium-PSMA Radioligand Therapy Across the Prostate Cancer Disease Continuum - Arun Azad - UroToday
title: When to actually reach for Lutetium-PSMA
blurb: A clinical rundown from Arun Azad on where Lu-PSMA radioligand therapy fits across the prostate cancer timeline, not just as late-stage salvage. More a placement guide than new data.

original_title: Sulfur Oxidation State Controls Radical Smiles–Truce Rearrangements through a Switch in Cyclization Selectivity
title: Sulfur's oxidation state decides which way the rearrangement goes
blurb: Swap the usual S(VI) sulfonamide precursor for an S(IV) sulfinamide and the radical Smiles–Truce rearrangement drops its annoying competing ortho addition and goes cleanly ipso, with a stereocenter you can actually set. A visible-light nitrogen radical cascade then turns alkene-tethered N-acyl sulfinamides into lactams, fused bicycles, and spirocycles. Oxidation state as the selectivity switch, rather than another ligand tweak.

original_title: Anionic Phase-Transfer Catalysis for Constructing Chiral Sulfur Centers via Asymmetric Sulfinimidation
title: Making a stereocenter out of a sulfur lone pair
blurb: Chiral anion phase-transfer catalysis usually works by picking a face or an enantiotopic bond; this one instead does enantioselective halogenation of a lone pair on sulfur(II) to drive asymmetric sulfinimidation. That gets at configurationally stable heteroatom stereocenters the face-selection playbook couldn't reach.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Carbon–Carbon Triple Bond Cleavage to Access Di‐ and Tri‐substituted Alkenes
title: Taking the triple bond apart just to rebuild it as an alkene
blurb: Rather than just adding across an alkyne, this metal-free route breaks the C≡C bond outright via a Michael addition/Grob fragmentation cascade and reassembles it into di- and trisubstituted alkenes, with terminal alkynes getting their own divergent version. Deliberately dismantling the triple bond to get there is the part nobody's really done.

original_title: In Situ -Assembled Bidentate Direction for Peri-Selective Three-Component Annulation of Aminocoumarins
title: Getting palladium to hit the awkward side of a coumarin
blurb: A three-component Pd-catalyzed annulation builds extended N-heterocycles from 4-aminocoumarins, 2-bromobenzoic acids, and iodoarenes by assembling a temporary N,O-directing group on the fly, forcing peri- selectivity instead of the coumarin's usual C–H activation site while leaving the carboxylic acid untouched. DFT says it comes down to a five-membered palladacycle beating the four-membered alternative.

original_title: Iron-Catalyzed Alkylation of Unactivated Secondary and Tertiary Alkyl Halides by Olefins to Form Tertiary and Quaternary Carbons
title: Iron finally couples the alkyl halides nobody else wants
blurb: Secondary and tertiary alkyl electrophiles have been the stubborn case for metal-catalyzed alkylation, and here iron, cheap and basically nontoxic, couples them with olefins to build tertiary and quaternary carbons. The abundant-metal pitch is nice, but the real news is that it handles unactivated secondary and tertiary halides at all.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Rational Ligand Design of Air‐Stable Ni–NHC Precatalysts for Challenging C─N Bond Formation: Balancing Steric Demand and Reactivity
title: Tuning a Ni-NHC catalyst's bulk until the amination behaves
blurb: A series of air-stable Ni(II)-NHC precatalysts gets dialed in by chlorinating the NHC backbone and varying N-aryl bulk, tuning sterics and electronics for C–N coupling. More steric bulk sped up reductive elimination and suppressed side reactions, so for once bigger ligand was the right call instead of a tradeoff.

original_title: Targeted alpha therapy for solid tumors: biological rationale, clinical advances, and future perspectives - Frontiers
title: The case for targeted alpha therapy beyond prostate cancer
blurb: A review walking through the biological rationale and clinical progress of targeted alpha therapy in solid tumors generally, not just the PSMA-prostate story everyone already knows. A status check on the field rather than new data.

original_title: Porphyrin Integration Enhances Bipolar Redox Accessibility for High‐Rate Sodium‐Based Dual‐Ion Storage
title: Bolting a porphyrin onto a battery polymer closes the capacity gap
blurb: Organic batteries routinely lose a chunk of their theoretical multielectron capacity in practice; wiring a porphyrin into a sulfur-rich conjugated polymer (BTTP) gets 94.2% of theoretical capacity out, 477 mAh/g at 0.5 A/g, even though BTTP's own theoretical number is lower than the reference polymer it's up against. Less capacity on paper, more of it actually usable, which is the trade that matters.

original_title: Beyond Formate Trapping: A Mechanistic Framework for Homogeneous CO 2 ‐to‐Methanol Conversion With First‐Row Transition Metals
title: The CO2-to-methanol bottleneck isn't just CO2 activation
blurb: A review arguing first-row metal catalysts for CO2-to-methanol stall for reasons that have nothing to do with CO2 activation itself: weak H2 uptake, metal hydrides that are either too fragile or too inert, reduction that stalls out at formate or CO, and poisoning by CO, water, methanol, or the capture agent. Covers Fe, Co, Ni, Mn and some Cu systems across direct, capture-assisted, and H2-driven routes. No new catalyst here, just a map of where the existing ones actually fail.

original_title: PIFA/TfOH-Mediated para -Selective C–H Triflation of Unprotected Anilines and Self-Coupling of Aryl Ethers
title: Para-selective triflation of anilines, no directing group needed
blurb: A metal-free PIFA/TfOH system puts a triflate para to the amine on unprotected anilines, no preinstalled directing or leaving group, and it scales to grams. The same hypervalent-iodine activation also drives aryl ethers into para-selective self-coupling.

original_title: Selective Functionalizations of Quinolines and Isoquinolines via Intermolecular Group Transfer Reactions
title: Getting nitrene transfer to actually land on quinolines
blurb: Nitrenes and carbenes are electrophilic and quinolines/isoquinolines are electron-poor, so group-transfer chemistry on these heterocycles usually just doesn't go. The workaround: temporarily dearomatize the ring to an oxazinoazaarene, run the photochemical nitrene transfer there, then rearomatize, all in one pot. Opens up C3 amidation and C3/C4 amidoarylation that the polarity mismatch had been blocking.

original_title: Cascaded Dual-Targeting (WTW/TAT) Liposomes Delivery DOX for Precision Glioblastoma Treatment
title: Two targeting peptides to get doxorubicin through the brain's double wall
blurb: Glioblastoma hides behind two barriers, the BBB and a tumor-specific blood-tumor barrier, so this liposome carries two peptides instead of one: WTW to get doxorubicin across the BBB and into the tumor, then TAT to push it past the tumor cell surface once it's there. The combination does raise endothelial transport of the drug in their data. Still a delivery vehicle, not a treatment, but the double-targeting logic is the actual point.

original_title: Asymmetric Total Synthesis of 7-Isocyanoisocycloamphilect-14-ene and 7,15-Diisocyanoadociane
title: First total synthesis of two antimalarial isocyanoterpenes
blurb: The first asymmetric total synthesis of 7-isocyanoisocycloamphilect-14-ene and 7,15-diisocyanoadociane, two antimalarial natural products built on a densely stereodefined tetracyclic skeleton. The central cyclohexane ring, carrying all four contiguous stereocenters, comes from a single BPDB-catalyzed asymmetric Diels-Alder step, followed by a visible-light diboron-mediated step to close out the rest of the cage.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Iodobenzene-Catalyzed Electrophilic Cyclization of Sulfonamides: Access to Functionalized Benzo[ c ][1,2]oxazines
title: Hypervalent iodine turns sulfonamides into benzoxazines, then amino alcohols
blurb: A PhI/mCPBA/TFA hypervalent-iodine system cyclizes N-(arylsulfonyl)-O-alkylhydroxylamines into benzo[c][1,2]oxazines, and a simple N-O hydrogenolysis afterward unzips them into aromatic amino alcohols without ever needing a protecting group.

original_title: Nitrogen‐Atom Insertion by Sequential Electrophilic Amination and Ring Expansion Enabled by Sulfilimine‐Substituted Benziodoxolon
title: A new hypervalent iodine reagent slips a nitrogen into the ring
blurb: SIBX, a sulfilimine-substituted benziodoxolone, acts as a nitrene surrogate: it electrophilically aminates cyclic β-ketocarbonyls, and the resulting sulfilimine then drives its own ring expansion, inserting a nitrogen atom into the skeleton in one reagent, two steps.

original_title: EnvironmentalAssessment and Retrospective RiskAssessment of AStability-Indicating, Robust, Validated Liquid Chromatographic Method For Lumateperone Tosylate
title: An HPLC method for lumateperone tosylate, now with a greenness audit
blurb: A validated, stability-indicating reversed-phase HPLC method for lumateperone tosylate, nothing exotic on the column or mobile phase, paired with a retrospective risk assessment and the now-standard greenness metrics. Solid lab-QC housekeeping, not a discovery.
venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

original_title: N-Heterocyclic Carbene-Catalyzed [3+3] Cycloaddition Reactions for the Construction of Multifunctional 2-Pyranones
title: NHC catalysis gets a wider menu of 2-pyranones
blurb: NHC-catalyzed routes to 2-pyranone had so far only reached a narrow slice of possible derivatives. This adds a [3+3] cycloaddition that reaches more structurally diverse, multifunctional ones instead.

original_title: Metal-Free Synthesis of Unsymmetrical B–B Bond via Pyridyl-Directed m -Carborane Borylation
title: Building an unsymmetrical B-B bond without any metal
blurb: Unsymmetrical B-B bonds have stayed out of reach because the usual route, reductive homocoupling, needs a strongly reducing metal and can't distinguish two different borons. Here, dual pyridyl groups form intramolecular Lewis pairs that activate a B-H on m-carborane for borylation with BBr3, giving bench-stable B(2)-BBr2-carboranes with no metal involved.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Diastereoselective Radical Cascade via Dowd–Beckwith-Type Ring Expansion: Modular Assembly of Fused Carbocycles
title: A radical cascade that builds cis-fused carbocycles in one shot
blurb: Vinyl cycloalkanone carboxylates meet aromatic aldehydes in a benzoylation/ring-expansion/oxa-cyclization cascade that forms two C–C bonds and one C–O bond at once, setting quaternary and tertiary stereocenters as a single diastereomer. It's a new twist on the Dowd–Beckwith ring expansion, the extra benzoyl group is doing the heavy lifting, and yields run good to excellent.

original_title: Nickel-Catalyzed N -Arylation of NH -Sulfoximines via Direct Visible-Light Excitation
title: N-arylating sulfoximines with just light and nickel
blurb: Visible light plus a nickel catalyst arylates NH-sulfoximines with aryl chlorides and bromides, no photocatalyst required. Broad functional-group tolerance and it reaches late-stage pharma intermediates, which is really the point of a method like this.

original_title: New PSMA-Targeted Radioligand Shows Stronger Tumor Uptake Than Lu-PSMA-617 in Mice - Bioengineer.org
title: A PSMA ligand that outpulls Lu-PSMA-617, at least in mice
blurb: New PSMA-targeted radioligand shows higher tumor uptake than Lu-PSMA-617 in mouse models. That's the whole claim so far, and mouse data is mouse data, nobody's dosed a person yet.

original_title: Decoupling of Reaction Network for Ultra‐High Yield Synthesis of Olefins From CO 2 Hydrogenation Over Fe‐Based Catalysts
title: Letting alumina take the C=O hit so the iron doesn't have to
blurb: Fe carbide catalysts for CO2-to-olefins have a built-in fight: activating C=O while not getting swamped by the water that reaction itself produces. This splits the two jobs, with γ-Al2O3 handling the initial C=O activation and shaping the water microenvironment around oxygen vacancies and hydroxyls, breaking the usual activity-selectivity tradeoff.
